target: β_D (deuteron canonical σ-word; total crossing count)
description: Atomic-braid recipe for the deuteron: derives the canonical 23-crossing σ-word β_D from first principles by composing the per-nucleon recipe chains (`atomic-braid-recipe-{p,n}.derivation.json`) with a single inter-nucleon mixed-flavour crossing at σ_2 (averaged interface, AXIOM).  Type breakdown {σ: 11, σ^{-1}: 7, averaged: 5} matches the canonical encoding from `canonical_braid_crossings.atom_canonical_crossings(Z=1, N=1, include_inter=True)`.  Trust profile is {axiom: 1, mathlib-cited: 0, derived: 3, script-cited: 0, computational: 1} — fully-trusted, zero SCRIPT_CITED.  Discharges the SCRIPT_CITED frontier on step 3 of `markov-trace-assembly-deuteron.derivation.json` (per D-tr-M-q0.derivation.json step 7 notes).  Companion to `atomic-braid-recipe-{p,n}.derivation.json`.

steps.name: Proton intra-nucleon word β_p at (σ_0, σ_1) — chain reference
steps.operation: Reference `atomic-braid-recipe-p.derivation.json`: the proton contributes its full 11-crossing word at the first nucleon's generator pair (σ_0, σ_1).  In the (c, d, gen_idx) encoding from `mass_at_3A_proper.atom_braid_word_3A`, this is 7 entries on σ_0 (gen 0) + 4 entries on σ_1 (gen 1).

steps.name: Inter-nucleon (p, n) crossing at σ_2
steps.operation: By the inter-nucleon coupling axiom, adjacent nucleons k and k+1 of opposite flavour (p, n) contribute a mixed-flavour crossing at gen 3k+2.  Per the operator-valued interface rule, mixed (p, n) flavours yield an averaged crossing: 1× (c=1, d=−h/2) at gen 2, with multiplicity m_pn = 1 (default).  Contributes 1 averaged entry to the σ-word.

steps.name: Neutron intra-nucleon word β_n at (σ_3, σ_4) — chain reference
steps.operation: Reference `atomic-braid-recipe-n.derivation.json`: the neutron contributes its full 11-crossing word at the second nucleon's generator pair (σ_3, σ_4).  In the (c, d, gen_idx) encoding from `mass_at_3A_proper.atom_braid_word_3A`, this is 7 entries on σ_3 (gen 3) + 4 entries on σ_4 (gen 4).

steps.name: Concatenate β_p ⊕ inter ⊕ β_n → β_D (canonical encoding)
steps.operation:
Concatenate the proton intra-nucleon word, the inter-nucleon mixed crossing, and the neutron intra-nucleon word in order:
  β_D = β_p[at (σ_0, σ_1)] + inter_pn[at σ_2] + β_n[at (σ_3, σ_4)]
Total entries: 11 + 1 + 11 = 23.
Type breakdown after merging:
  σ:        6 (proton) + 0 + 5 (neutron)        = 11
  σ^{-1}:   3 (proton) + 0 + 4 (neutron)        = 7
  averaged: 2 (proton) + 1 (inter) + 2 (neutron) = 5
Matches `canonical_braid_crossings.atom_canonical_crossings(Z=1, N=1, include_inter=True)`.

steps.name: Emit β_D σ-word (computational leaf)
steps.operation: Run `canonical_braid_crossings.atom_canonical_crossings(Z=1, N=1, include_inter=True)`; verify the output is a list of 23 (gen_idx, ctype) pairs matching the breakdown from step 4.
steps.notes: Cross-check: `len(atom_canonical_crossings(Z=1, N=1, include_inter=True)) == 23`.  Type breakdown from the actual call: {sigma: 11, sigma_inv: 7, averaged: 5} — matches step 4 derivation.
